extensions.claim_text: Hudson has a $75M asset-based revolving credit facility with Wells Fargo Bank expiring March 2027, with FY24 working capital of $147.7M, cash of $70.1M (up from $12.4M YoY), no debt outstanding, $91.8
extensions.source_label: Wells Fargo asset-based lending public commitment data (8-K Item 1.01 exhibits)
extensions.endpoint_or_method: EDGAR — pull credit agreement exhibits from 8-Ks dated 2022-03-02 (Amended A&R), 2024-06-06 (First Amendment), 2024-10-23 (Second Amendment)
extensions.rationale: ABL covenant structure (minimum-liquidity, springing FCCR, repurchase carve-outs) is the canonical lender-side signal for borrower stress. The Second Amendment expanded buyback capacity — that is an UPGRADE not a distress signal.
extensions.expected_observable: credit-agreement covenants showing maintained liquidity headroom and increasing buyback permissions
extensions.signal_direction: covenant relaxation in favor of buyback corroborates non-distress; covenant tightening or waivers would signal distress

extensions.rationale: Insider behavior is a cross-check on the management's optimism vs. distress; in a genuine going-concern setup we would expect heavy insider selling, while in this case officers/directors own ~8% per the 10-K.
